description:
Rydzyna Castle stands beside the market square of Rydzyna, a small town in southern Greater Poland about 60 km south of Poznań. A Gothic stronghold occupied the site from the early 15th century, built by Jan of Czernina, but the building visitors encounter today owes its character to a complete rebuilding at the end of the 17th century: Italian architects, among them Giuseppe Simone Bellotti and later Pompeo Ferrari, transformed it into a Baroque castle for the Leszczyński family.

The castle's royal chapter came soon after. Stanisław Leszczyński, later King of Poland, lived at Rydzyna between 1704 and 1709, a residence cut short when the castle was partly burned in 1709 during the Great Northern War. Ownership later passed to the Sułkowski family — sources differ on exactly when this happened, so no precise year is given here — who added Rococo interiors and turned Rydzyna into a genuine cultural centre for the wider Greater Poland region.

The Sułkowski line ended with the death of the last prince in 1909, after which the castle passed to the Prussian state and became a school. It was burned in January 1945, in the final stages of the Second World War, leaving the building in ruins. From 1970, the Association of Polish Mechanical Engineers and Technicians undertook a long rebuilding, completed in 1989 and based on pre-war documentation; the restoration won a Europa Nostra award in 1994, and in 2017 the castle and town ensemble together were named a Historic Monument of Poland.

Today the castle operates as a hotel and conference centre, with its reconstructed Baroque and Rococo halls open to guided tours alongside the overnight accommodation.

faqs.question: Did King Stanisław Leszczyński really live at Rydzyna Castle?
faqs.answer: Yes — he lived there between 1704 and 1709, before later becoming King of Poland. His residence ended when the castle was partly burned in 1709 during the Great Northern War.

faqs.question: Is the castle's interior original or rebuilt?
faqs.answer: Rebuilt. The castle was burned in January 1945, and the halls visitors see today are the result of a reconstruction carried out from 1970 to 1989 by the Association of Polish Mechanical Engineers and Technicians, based on pre-war documentation. The restoration won a Europa Nostra award in 1994.

hotel.how_to_stay:
**Getting there:** In the town of Rydzyna in southern Greater Poland, about 60 km south of Poznań, reached by road; the castle stands beside the market square.

**Rooms & rates:** From approx. €89/night for a 15 m² double, with a 30 m² Large Double from around €100 and a 46 m² Standard Apartment from around €109; breakfast is included and free cancellation is available on the rates seen.

**On-site:** The hotel also has a restaurant and conference facilities, and the reconstructed historic halls can be visited on a guided tour (confirm current hours locally).

**Good to know:** Rydzyna is run by an engineers' association as a hotel and conference centre, so weekday stays may coincide with events. The interiors you see are a reconstruction completed in 1989, based on pre-war documentation.

**Combine with:** [Kórnik Castle](/castles/poland/kornik-castle) and [Rogalin Palace](/castles/poland/rogalin-palace) near Poznań.
